Latin word

peccātum

peccātum, peccātī n.

noun, second declension

a fault, a slip; a sin, a wrong

In this lexicon

  • mistake

    also used · classical · Publ. P 62: Peccātum extenuat, quī celeriter corrigit.

  • sin

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. And. 903: Prō peccātō magnō paulum supplicī satis est patrī; Cic. Fin. 3.32 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Pater, peccāvī in caelum, et cōram tē: jam nōn sum dignus vocārī fīlius tuus.

    Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son.Vulg. Lc. 15.21

    What have I done? What have I deserved, what wrong have I done, father?Ter. And. 139

    such a little boy and such a great sinnerAug. Conf. 1.12.19

  • Deus propitius estō mihi peccātōrī.

    God, be merciful to me, a sinner.Vulg. Lc. 18.13
